# S8 — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping`: live Jira probe to pre-populate mapping config

## Context / Problem
Epic 3d7a (S1–S5) adds the config-driven mapping seam: a reserved `[mapping]` /
`[tool.rebar.mapping]` block with per-layer vocabulary (`statuses`, `issue_types`,
`link_types`, `hierarchy`) and axis maps (`status_map`, `type_map`, `link_map`,
`priority_map`, `create_defaults`), parsed by
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py` (S1). Authoring that block by
hand is transcription-error-prone. S8 adds a READ-ONLY command that observes a live
Jira project over REST and emits a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block seeded with
the project's real vocabulary, identity-seed axis maps, and `create_defaults` stubs.

Blocking findings resolved here:
- The originally-proposed verb `rebar bridge probe` COLLIDES with the retired
  compatibility alias `bridge-probe`, registered at `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:579`
  and `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py:117` (`check-access`), whose handler
  `_bridge_probe` (`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:103`) runs `jira-capability-probe.py`
  and CREATES+DELETES a throwaway issue — not read-only. Held-out/vocabulary tests
  assert that alias. New verb: **`rebar bridge suggest-mapping`** (verified free across
  `src/` and `tests/`).
- The repo has NO tomlkit; TOML is read with stdlib `tomllib` and the ONLY writer is
  `src/rebar/_config_writer.py` (`_emit_toml` + `write_jira_config`), which emits a
  single level of `[section]`. So `--write` cannot preserve inline comments and needs
  the emitter extended for nested tables. Scoped honestly below.

## Approach
Add a read-only probe under a new `suggest-mapping` verb wired into the bridge command
group (NEW):
- Parser: a `commands.add_parser("suggest-mapping", ...)` entry in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py` (beside `check-access` at line ~117),
  accepting `<PROJECT>` and `--write`.
- Dispatch: add `"suggest-mapping"` to the pass-through set in `bridge_cli`
  (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:259`) and a branch in `_passthrough` /
  `_passthrough_help` forwarding to a NEW handler `_bridge_suggest_mapping`
  (`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, sibling of `_bridge_probe`).

Probe (NEW module `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_probe.py`, <800 LOC):
issue GETs against the endpoints the live PoC proved — `/project/{key}/statuses`,
`/issuetype` (read `hierarchyLevel`), `/issueLinkType`, `/priority`, and
`/issue/createmeta/{key}/issuetypes/{id}` — via a small injected probe port
`get_json(path)`. The default port wraps the pycontribs `jira.JIRA` client's
`_get_json`, built through the existing `_jira_client_class()` seam in
`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:131` (monkeypatchable exactly like that seam, so
tests inject a FAKE REST client). Map results to a `MappingLayer`-shaped dict:
discovered vocabulary lists + `hierarchy`; identity-seed `status_map`/`type_map`/
`link_map`/`priority_map` (local key → same-named target VALUE); `create_defaults`
stubs (below).

Emit: build a `{"projects": {<KEY>: {...}}}` mapping dict.
- Default (no `--write`): serialize just that block to stdout as TOML. NEVER writes.
- `--write`: mirror `write_jira_config`'s proven read-whole/mutate/re-emit/atomic-
  replace pattern. Target selection reuses `config._discover_project_config` → an
  existing `rebar.toml`, else create `<repo_root>/rebar.toml`; a user `pyproject.toml`
  is NEVER edited. Read the target with `tomllib`, DEEP-MERGE the suggestion under
  `[mapping.projects.<KEY>]` with EXISTING keys winning (hand edits never clobbered),
  re-emit whole, atomic `os.replace`.

Serialization mechanism (concrete): extend `_config_writer._emit_toml` to recurse into
nested dict tables, emitting dotted headers (`[mapping.projects.KEY.status_map]`),
since today it stops at one level. No new dependency (stdlib `tomllib` read only).
HONEST SCOPE: because `tomllib` drops comments and there is no tomlkit, the deep-merge
preserves existing hand-edited VALUES (data-level, existing keys win) but inline
comments/formatting in the `[mapping]` block are NOT preserved on a `--write`. This is
documented in the command help and matches the existing `_emit_toml` contract
("comments are not preserved").

## Scope
- NEW `mapping_probe.py` (probe port + endpoint reads + layer builder + TOML emit),
  under the 800-LOC cap.
- Extend `src/rebar/_config_writer.py` `_emit_toml` for nested tables (kept < cap).
- Wire the verb: `bridge.py` parser, `_bridge_commands.py` dispatch, `__init__.py`
  handler `_bridge_suggest_mapping` (NEW).
- `create_defaults` stubs are createmeta fields with `required: true` whose id/name is
  NOT already in the outbound create baseline (see Acceptance).
- Out of scope: any WRITE to Jira; live-credential CI gating; comment round-tripping.

## Testing
Automated tests use a FAKED probe port (canned JSON for the five endpoints) — fully
offline, no live Jira/CI credential (rebar portability rule). A live smoke run is
manual only, never a CI gate. New tests in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `test_probe_emits_mapping` — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping <KEY>` against the fake
      port emits a `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block containing discovered vocabulary
      (`statuses`/`issue_types`/`link_types`/`hierarchy`), identity-seed axis maps, and
      `create_defaults` stubs.
- [ ] `test_probe_is_read_only` — default invocation writes NO file and issues only GETs
      (fake port records no create/delete), distinct from `check-access`.
- [ ] `test_probe_write_preserves_edits` — `--write` deep-merges under
      `projects.<KEY>`; a pre-existing hand-edited key in the target `rebar.toml` keeps
      its value (existing keys win); `pyproject.toml` is never edited.
- [ ] `test_probe_transitions_best_effort` — the Jira API returns transitions only from
      the current status, so the emitted `status_map` / transition hints are flagged
      best-effort (comment/partial marker), not asserted complete.

"create_defaults" baseline (concrete): the outbound create path
`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:140-158` (`map_local_to_remote`) already supplies
`summary`, `description`, `issuetype`, `priority`, `assignee`, and conditionally
`status` and `parent`. A `create_defaults` stub is emitted ONLY for a createmeta
`required: true` field whose id/name is NOT in that baseline set.

Test tier: unit
